ground_truth.location: Table 4, International terrorist attack (All countries, attacks with more than 15 deaths)
ground_truth.context: Table 4 ("Effect of Terrorist Attacks on Executive Approval Ratings").  Linear regression on time-series cross-sectional data of country-quarters: the percentage of the public approving of the executive in the quarter following the attack, regressed on an indicator for a major international terrorist attack (an attack with an international component under the Global Terrorism Database's definition and more than 15 deaths), the presence of a woman executive, their interaction, and controls for GDP growth, logged inflation, the left-center-right placement of the leader and elections, with country fixed effects and panel-corrected standard errors.  Sample: countries in the executive approval database that also appear in the Global Terrorism Database, 1975-2017.  This coefficient is the attack effect for men executives (the rally).

ground_truth.location: Table 4, International terrorist attack x Woman executive
ground_truth.context: Table 4, the paper's global test of the gender-revised rally framework: the coefficient on the interaction of a major international terrorist attack (more than 15 deaths) with a woman executive, in the same linear country-quarter regression of next-quarter executive approval (controls for woman executive, GDP, logged inflation, left-center-right placement of the leader and elections; country fixed effects; panel-corrected standard errors). Negative and significant at the 5% level in the paper.

i4r.notes: Coding error fixed: the election-quarter covariates (current quarter and four lags).  DP41 Table 1 Panel A col 6 / meta-database row "Fixing election quarter coding errors": -3.452 (SE 1.821), p = 0.058, N = 4,429 — no longer significant at 5%.  DP41 re-coded elections from public sources (60 contemporaneous observations changed; 317 amendments across the lags: US elections missing, Japan's upper house missing, run-offs and multi-round elections coded in one quarter only, errors for Austria 2016q4, Ecuador 1997q4, Iceland 2008q2/2012q2, Mexico 1991q3, Paraguay 2000q3, Turkey 2014q3).  Other DP41 variants (robustness, not corrections): no election controls -2.992 (1.841); no controls -2.650 (1.812); excluding the May-Manchester quarter -3.279 (1.982), and with corrected elections too -2.390 (1.945); country-clustered xtreg -3.194 (p = 0.558).  Authors' corrigendum (updated data, 14+ deaths threshold): -3.910 (1.798), N = 4,612.

The corrigendum's re-built panel has 4,612.

ground_truth.location: Table 2, column May likeability, Manchester attack * time
ground_truth.context: Table 2 ("Difference-in-Difference, with Fixed Effects"), May likeability column.  British Election Study internet panel, using waves before and after the 22 May 2017 Manchester Arena bombing. Outcome: how much the respondent likes Theresa May, 0 (strongly dislike) to 10 (strongly like).  Regressors: Manchester attack (the respondent was surveyed after the attack in the attack wave, wave 12), time (0 for waves before the attack, 1 for waves from 12 onward), their interaction (the coefficient here), wave fixed effects, and controls for identifying as ethnically British, gender, Labour party membership, other party membership, income and ideology.  OLS according to the table note; standard errors in parentheses.

i4r.notes: DP41 Table B1 col 1: -0.1274 (0.0187), N = 143,499, reproduced exactly; DP41 corrects nothing in the likeability model.  (The authors' 2024 corrigendum later restricts it to waves 9-12: -0.3273 (0.0255), N = 79,619.)

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=-0.0996072 vs claimed=-0.1274 (relative error 21.82%, tolerance 14.68%, the ±1·SE band with SE=0.0187).

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Table 4: coefficients are from OLS with country (country_code) dummies; panel-corrected SEs are computed by hand (Beck-Katz, casewise) since no PCSE package is installed. Coefficients do not depend on the SE method. No AR(1)/Prais-Winsten correction was applied because the paper does not mention one.

Table 4: DV is lag_approval (the only approval variable, labelled 'Lagged approval'); attack indicator is kill_16 (international attack with 16+ deaths, i.e. more than 15; exactly 60 country-quarters, 9 under women executives as the paper states); execrlc entered linearly; 'growth' is used as stored (it is a real-GDP level series). The estimation sample has 44 country-office units, not the 66 the paper mentions (country_code takes only 44 distinct values in the data).

Table 2: all waves with a non-missing outcome are used (like May: waves 9-16; best PM: waves 7, 8, 10, 11, 12); likeMayW code 9999 (don't know) set to missing; outcome for best PM is bestPMW (1 = May, 0 = Corbyn), logit; controls white, gender, labour, party_other, income, ideology2 (ideology with missing coded to the scale midpoint); no survey weights. time is perfectly collinear with the wave dummies, so time is entered before them and the last wave dummy (16 for like May, 12 for best PM) is dropped; the reported Time coefficient depends on this choice.
cell.notes: Independent blind reproduction from the paper text and data files only (the readme .docx in the mount was read for file descriptions; replication_files.do is listed in metadata.json but is not in the mount and was not read). attempt-1 and attempt-2 were exploratory (variable inventories, codings, missingness); attempt-3 crashed in the hand-rolled PCSE step (singular X'X because GDP is on a ~1e7 scale) and was fixed by inverting via QR. Caveats: the Table 4 regression's R2 (0.268) is well below the R2 printed in the paper's Table 4 note, and the interaction is not significant under our PCSE (the paper says it is significant at 5%), so the paper's Table 4 specification probably differs in some way the text does not describe (e.g. sample, an xtpcse option, or variable construction). Per blind rules the specification was not adjusted toward any reported figure.
